scope_note: Daily edition from matching Tuesday /new listings: 313 non-replacement cs.CV rows, 116 cs.RO rows, 409 deduplicated papers, and 336 ROI papers. Tier A cards use the repository parser abstracts and official arXiv HTML availability checks for the selected papers.
executive_thesis: The August 11 batch says the next robotics advantage is not a larger perception backbone; it is the instrumented interface between evidence, latent state, adaptation, and action. LIRA opens the VLM-to-action routing problem, GWM-VLA and SLIM ask which predictive latents are actually action-grounded, VANE and SC2-WM turn deployment feedback into selective correction, CMU-Drive and FactorDrive make driving reasoning conditional on cooperation and planning-critical factors, and EndoMD-SLAM shows that a map must know when not to update. APRL should treat every memory, world model, compressed token, and safety claim as a contract: which downstream action changes, under which stress condition, and what evidence would force us to stop using it.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: Action interfaces are now first-class model components
decision_cards.body: LIRA, SLIM, JEPA-WAM, and World Tokens all focus on the interface that converts visual-language representations into executable robot actions, not just the upstream encoder.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: Online adaptation needs delayed evidence
decision_cards.body: VANE, SC2-WM, SAFE-CHEM, and RecoverFly ask whether a correction should be committed only after future observations, uncertainty, or failure replay support it.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: Benchmarks must attack shortcut variables
decision_cards.body: EMRD, Evidence-RL, consequence-sensitive compression, and EndoMD-SLAM all separate useful evidence from priors, nuisance conditions, or transient artifacts that can silently corrupt a decision.

papers.title: LIRA: Local Cross-Layer Information Routing for Vision-Language-Action Decoding
papers.fit: VLA action decoding - representation routing - deployment transfer
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv abstract and HTML availability checked
papers.status_quo: VLA action decoders often consume a narrow or rigid slice of the pretrained VLM hierarchy.
papers.friction: A robot action can depend on low-level geometry, mid-level affordance, and high-level task tokens at the same control step.
papers.hidden_premise: Layer-local routing can expose complementary evidence without changing the backbone or the supervised training recipe.
papers.conceptual_move: Treat VLM-to-action conditioning as depth-aware local information routing into parallel fusion blocks.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes task-token features, LIRA query features from intermediate states, and proprioceptive fusion before action prediction.

evidence.claim: The paper identifies the VLM-to-action routing interface as underexplored.
It reports an 18.9-point zero-shot transfer gain on LIBERO-Plus over VLA-Adapter under the same 0.5B configuration.
APRL should log which encoder depths change each action under viewpoint and object-shift splits.

papers.falsification: If the same layers route under every task phase, LIRA is an adapter regularizer rather than a state-sensitive interface.
papers.adversarial: A local layer window may overfit benchmark phase structure; transfer needs novel camera pose, object layout, and contact-state shifts.
papers.thinking_tool: Ask which representation depth changed the motor command, not only which backbone produced the embedding.
papers.transfer_boundary: Direct for VLA manipulation; weaker for modular systems whose action decoder already receives explicit state estimates.

papers.title: GWM-VLA: Geometry-Aware Latent World Modeling for Vision-Language-Action Learning
papers.fit: geometry-aware world model - multi-view latent state - action supervision
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv abstract and HTML availability checked
papers.status_quo: Latent VLA world models can predict view dynamics while treating camera views as independent evidence streams.
papers.friction: Manipulation robustness under visual shift depends on end-effector geometry and gripper-object interaction, not holistic scene prediction alone.
papers.hidden_premise: Multi-view aggregation and action supervision can force the latent transition to preserve geometry that matters for control.
papers.conceptual_move: Aggregate multi-view observations into geometry-aware states, predict target-view patch tokens, and share latent-action representations with the action head.
papers.mechanism: The abstract names VGGT-Omega aggregation, target wrist-view prediction, and flow-matching action supervision as the coupled path.

evidence.claim: Existing latent world models are described as weak at explicitly modeling geometric relationships across camera views.
The proposed latent representation is grounded by both next-view prediction and robot-action supervision.
APRL should probe whether latent geometry predicts contact error before final task success changes.

papers.falsification: If geometry-aware latents improve view prediction but not action recovery under camera shift, the geometry is not operational.
papers.adversarial: Targeting the wrist view can hide failures in global scene state, so static-camera and wrist-camera ablations should be separated.
papers.thinking_tool: World-model quality should be measured by the geometry variable a controller consumes.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for manipulation with multi-view observations; less direct for single-camera policies without calibrated view geometry.

papers.title: VANE: Reliable Test-Time Training for Vision-Language-Action Models via Future Visual Representation Prediction
papers.fit: VLA test-time training - selective update - future evidence
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv abstract and HTML availability checked
papers.status_quo: Deployment-time adaptation often updates a shared policy space before the consequence of that update is known.
papers.friction: Closed-loop manipulation can be damaged by a correction that mixes incompatible task errors or commits too early.
papers.hidden_premise: Adaptation should be isolated from the live policy and committed only when future visual observations support the update.
papers.conceptual_move: Use future visual representation prediction as delayed evidence for selective, reversible prompt adaptation.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes candidate updates isolated from the live policy, evaluated on later observations, then committed only when supported.

evidence.claim: The paper states that online updates can alter subsequent actions before their consequences are known.
It reports a 3.2 percentage-point average success gain over a corresponding TTT baseline on SimplerEnv WidowX.
APRL should maintain an adaptation quarantine log before changing the deployed policy.

papers.falsification: If future-evidence gating only accepts easy corrections, it may improve average success while avoiding the rare failures that matter.
papers.adversarial: Future visual support can reward visually plausible but contact-wrong behavior unless contact and action residuals are also logged.
papers.thinking_tool: Do not let a model update itself until a later observation has audited the proposed correction.
papers.transfer_boundary: Direct for closed-loop VLA policies with unlabeled deployment streams; less direct for static offline evaluation.

papers.title: SLIM-0.5B: Learning Action-Grounded Predictive Latents for Robot Manipulation
papers.fit: compact VLA - predictive latent - low-latency manipulation
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv abstract and HTML availability checked
papers.status_quo: Large VLA backbones spend capacity on open-domain semantics even when manipulation needs compact transition variables.
papers.friction: Pixel-level world prediction can be expensive and can preserve visual detail that does not change control.
papers.hidden_premise: A smaller model can compete if its latent space is explicitly grounded in action-conditioned future transitions and inverse action explanation.
papers.conceptual_move: Train masked trajectory prediction with action reconstruction and future-latent prediction in a compact mixture-of-transformers backbone.
papers.mechanism: The abstract says SLIM captures both action-conditioned transitions and the actions that explain observed changes, then uses flow matching for actions.

evidence.claim: The paper argues continuous manipulation primarily requires compact observation-action-transition representations.
It claims competitive simulation and real-world performance with fewer parameters, lower latency, and lower GPU memory.
APRL should compare latent transition error against real action correction, not only model size.

papers.falsification: If latency improves but failure modes shift to unseen objects or contacts, compactness traded away necessary state.
papers.adversarial: A 0.5B result can benefit from task distribution fit; evaluate out-of-family object geometry and contact timing.
papers.thinking_tool: Compression is useful only after naming which action-relevant variable survives.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for manipulation policies where transition labels are available; weaker for language-heavy embodied tasks.

papers.title: SC2-WM: A Self-Correcting World Model with Closed-Loop Feedback for Vision-and-Language Navigation in Continuous Environments
papers.fit: VLN-CE - self-correcting world model - state drift feedback
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv abstract and HTML availability checked
papers.status_quo: VLN-CE policies often execute open loop under partial observability and detect failure only after navigation has drifted.
papers.friction: A route can look locally plausible while the internal state has already diverged from the instruction and observed layout.
papers.hidden_premise: World-model foresight can generate feedback before action execution and can trigger model-level correction at test time.
papers.conceptual_move: Use internal closed-loop feedback for state-level plan refinement, then selectively update the world model when feedback exposes capacity insufficiency.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes self-correction through world-model foresight and conditional world-aware adaptation.

evidence.claim: The paper names internal state drift during inference as the central VLN-CE failure.
It uses feedback before action execution and selective world-model test-time updates.
APRL should log when a predicted next observation disagrees with the actual one before wrong turns accumulate.

papers.falsification: If correction triggers after the same step as task failure, the feedback is diagnostic but not control-relevant.
papers.adversarial: World-model foresight can inherit map priors and mask localization drift; evaluate unseen layouts and ambiguous turns.
papers.thinking_tool: Treat navigation world models as drift sensors before treating them as planners.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for VLN and object navigation; less direct for manipulation unless future observations can be tied to contact state.

papers.title: Explore, Map, Remember, Decide: Are Embodied VLMs Ready for Safety-Critical Scenarios?
papers.fit: embodied VLM safety - spatial memory - bias under partial observability
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv abstract and HTML availability checked
papers.status_quo: Embodied VLMs can appear capable by producing plausible decisions without proving spatial memory or evidence grounding.
papers.friction: Safety-critical evacuation decisions can be driven by textual priors rather than the explored physical environment.
papers.hidden_premise: A safety benchmark must separate exploration coverage, map fidelity, memory persistence, and focal decision quality.
papers.conceptual_move: Extend Theory of Space into an Explore-Map-Remember-Decide pipeline with coverage, fidelity, memory, and decision metrics.
papers.mechanism: The abstract reports that VLMs often choose evacuation points from pre-trained textual priors and lose spatial reasoning in low light.

evidence.claim: The paper tests whether decisions are based on physical evidence or visual-language bias.
It reports divergence from human memory patterns and degraded spatial reasoning in low-light conditions.
APRL should score embodied policies by evidence-grounded memory, not final instruction answer alone.

papers.falsification: If focal decisions improve without map fidelity or memory persistence, the benchmark may still reward response priors.
papers.adversarial: The ToS task may not cover manipulation or locomotion hazards; include dynamic obstacles and irreversible actions before generalizing.
papers.thinking_tool: Split a safety decision into explore, map, remember, and decide, then attack each stage separately.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for navigation and safety-critical reasoning; weaker for low-level control unless connected to action authority.

papers.title: CMU-Drive and V2V-VLA: Cooperative Multi-agent Unified Driving with Reasoning Benchmark and Vehicle-to-Vehicle Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.fit: cooperative driving - multi-agent VLA - closed-loop benchmark
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv abstract and HTML availability checked
papers.status_quo: End-to-end driving VLA work is usually framed around an individual vehicle with local perception and planning.
papers.friction: Safety-critical traffic scenes require communication and cooperative perception, so single-agent reasoning hides coordination failure.
papers.hidden_premise: Driving actions, future waypoints, language reasoning, and communication policy can be generated in one cooperative forward pass.
papers.conceptual_move: Create a closed-loop cooperative driving benchmark and a V2V-VLA baseline for connected autonomous vehicles.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes CMU-Drive and V2V-VLA jointly generating actions, waypoints, reasoning, and communication policies.

evidence.claim: The paper frames cooperative autonomous driving as a missing benchmark and baseline.
It requires multiple connected vehicles in safety-critical scenarios with background traffic.
APRL should evaluate whether communication changes the action, not just whether the message is plausible.

papers.falsification: If vehicle-to-vehicle language does not improve closed-loop safety under occlusion or conflicting intent, it is explanatory overhead.
papers.adversarial: Communication can leak simulator priors; test delayed, missing, and adversarial messages separately.
papers.thinking_tool: A cooperative VLA must prove which partner evidence changed the ego action.
papers.transfer_boundary: Direct for driving and multi-robot systems; less direct for single-arm manipulation.

papers.title: EndoMD-SLAM: Endoscopic Gaussian Splatting SLAM under Optical Degradation with Memory and Static-Transient Decomposition
papers.fit: medical SLAM - transient artifact rejection - memory-gated mapping
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv abstract and HTML availability checked
papers.status_quo: Gaussian Splatting SLAM assumes multi-view photometric consistency and can fuse temporary artifacts into a persistent map.
papers.friction: Endoscopic debris and water flushing move with the camera, corrupting tracking and mapping if treated as anatomy.
papers.hidden_premise: A SLAM system should sometimes suspend updates and isolate transient fields rather than always integrate observations.
papers.conceptual_move: Use memory-driven tracking gates for unreliable observations and static-transient decomposition for mapping.
papers.mechanism: The abstract reports drift-aware relocalization from historical keyframes and a separate transient field for contaminants.

evidence.claim: The paper names camera-attached artifacts as a cause of irreversible map corruption.
It reports 91 percent absolute trajectory error reduction and 9.9 dB PSNR improvement under severe degradation.
APRL should test when mapping should reject observations rather than improve reconstruction loss.

papers.falsification: If gates only work for colonoscopy-specific artifacts, the static-transient split may not transfer to general robot mapping.
papers.adversarial: A memory gate can preserve stale geometry after real scene change; dynamic-update tests are required.
papers.thinking_tool: A map update is an action with a stop condition, not a passive accumulation step.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for SLAM under corruption and medical navigation; weaker for static offline reconstruction.

synthesis.title: Predictive latents and action decoders are converging
synthesis.links: LIRA - GWM-VLA - SLIM - JEPA-WAM - World Tokens
synthesis.facts: The papers separately route intermediate VLM layers, ground latent transitions with action supervision, and remove online world-model cost after training.
synthesis.inference: APRL should benchmark the interface variable that changes action: layer depth, latent transition, world token, or action expert state.

synthesis.title: Adaptation is becoming an evidence contract
synthesis.facts: The papers gate adaptation with future observations, self-correcting world-model feedback, uncertainty switching, or failure replay.
synthesis.inference: The deployment question is when to commit an update, who holds authority before commitment, and which future evidence invalidates it.

synthesis.title: Safety benchmarks now separate evidence from priors
synthesis.links: EMRD - Evidence-RL - consequence-sensitive token compression - EndoMD-SLAM
synthesis.facts: The batch tests physical evidence use, causal evidence regions, consequence-aware token budgets, and transient map corruption.
synthesis.inference: Robot evaluation should attack the shortcut variable before trusting a policy, descriptor, map, or compressed perception stack.

frontier_memory.label: Strengthening
frontier_memory.history: August 10 emphasized state accountability in VLA, world models, intervention, and geometry.
frontier_memory.body: August 11 strengthens that axis with action routing, future-evidence TTT, self-correcting navigation, and memory-gated SLAM.

frontier_memory.label: New signal
frontier_memory.history: Recent RI editions treated world models mostly as latent or rollout evaluators.
frontier_memory.body: Today adds a stronger interface question: can a world-model latent be shared with the action head without carrying irrelevant prediction detail?

frontier_memory.label: Missing axis
frontier_memory.history: Prior driving and navigation notes focused on single-agent or single-robot execution.
frontier_memory.body: CMU-Drive and EMRD add cooperation and safety-critical memory as axes that should be stressed explicitly.

strategy.title: Action-interface audit for VLA policies
strategy.thesis: Measure which representation depth, latent transition, and world token changes the action under controlled visual, semantic, and contact shifts.
strategy.one_week: Run one LIBERO-style replay with layer-depth routing logs, latent prediction loss, action delta, and contact-state labels.
strategy.four_week: Compare VLA-Adapter, LIRA-style routing, latent WAM, and compact predictive-latent policies on the same shift suite.
strategy.success: At least two interface signals predict different failure families before task-level success changes.
strategy.stop: Interface logs collapse to model confidence and do not change recovery or transfer ranking.
strategy.asset: Layer routing traces, world-token dumps, action deltas, contact labels, and shift-conditioned success tables.

strategy.title: Future-evidence adaptation quarantine
strategy.thesis: Treat test-time updates as untrusted candidates until later observations, world-model feedback, or uncertainty thresholds prove they should enter the live controller.
strategy.one_week: Implement a quarantine buffer that stores proposed prompt/model updates and replays the next observation before commit.
strategy.four_week: Evaluate VANE-style gating, SC2-WM correction, and uncertainty switching under object shifts, low light, and recovery tasks.
strategy.success: Gating reduces harmful updates while preserving at least half of the positive adaptation gain.
strategy.stop: Delayed evidence accepts only easy updates or fails to predict recoverability.
strategy.asset: Candidate-update logs, future-observation support scores, rejection labels, and operator handoff traces.

strategy.title: Shortcut-resistant robot evidence benchmark
strategy.thesis: Stress maps, VLM answers, token budgets, and driving communication with nuisance variables that look plausible but should not change the action.
strategy.one_week: Create a small suite with transient visual artifacts, low-light navigation, token-budget cost labels, and delayed V2V messages.
strategy.four_week: Evaluate SLAM, embodied VLM, VLA driving, and VLM compression methods by action change, not only answer or reconstruction quality.
strategy.success: The benchmark reverses at least one method ranking relative to a standard metric.
strategy.stop: Nuisance labels do not reveal failures beyond ordinary held-out splits.
strategy.asset: Artifact-corrupted videos, EMRD-style memory traces, cost-tagged VQA tasks, V2V message perturbations, and closed-loop action logs.
